title: The MIND model a microlearning AI-integrated instructional design for enhanced learning outcomes
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of how to design effective microlearning experiences that integrate AI in ways that improve learning outcomes. The authors argue that existing instructional design frameworks, especially ADDIE, are too rigid, linear, and insufficiently responsive to learner needs in technology-rich contexts. To address this, they developed the Microlearning AI-Integrated Instructional Design (MIND) model, grounded in TPACK and a factors-influencing-learning-outcomes framework, and then tested it empirically.

The intervention compared microlearning modules designed with the MIND model against the same course designed with ADDIE. The course, "Mastering AI-Powered Research Skills," was delivered through an AI-enabled OpenLearning platform and included 12 micro-modules on GenAI concepts, AI-assisted research, search optimization, reading support, data analysis, ethics, bias, and privacy. The study used a mixed-methods design: quantitative pretest-posttest comparisons with ANCOVA and demographic analyses, plus qualitative learner reflections on media richness, interaction, engagement, comprehension, motivation, satisfaction, and accessibility.

Participants were 64 learners at C3L, Universiti Brunei Darussalam, split evenly between experimental and control groups. The experimental group received modules designed with MIND and the educators involved received workshops to support MIND-based design; the control group received comparable content designed with ADDIE and delivered through blended/Canvas-based instruction. The results showed that the MIND condition produced significantly higher post-test scores than ADDIE, with no gender, locality, or employment-status differences within the MIND group, though younger learners benefited more. The authors conclude that the MIND model is a flexible, cost-effective, learner-centred approach for AI-integrated microlearning, though it still needs better support for peer interaction and longer-term evaluation.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a peer-reviewed mixed-methods quasi-experimental comparison with pre/post testing and ANCOVA, but it is not randomized at the learner level and includes a custom-developed intervention rather than a standardized implementation. Credibility is moderate-to-good, with quantitative and qualitative triangulation, though external validity is limited by the single-site, single-course context.
impact_tier_rationale: The intervention showed a large practical effect on post-test outcomes (partial η2=.430) relative to ADDIE, which exceeds the threshold for medium/large impact. The positive effects were observed across a general learner sample in a real educational setting, supporting a blue impact tier despite the non-K-12 context.

interventions.use_case: AI-integrated microlearning module design and delivery for a course on AI-powered research skills, delivered through an AI-enabled OpenLearning platform with videos, podcasts, slides, and PDFs.

GenAI tools such as ChatGPT, NotebookLM, Perplexity, and related AI tools used by the educator to generate, refine, and tailor microlearning content and support learner practice/feedback within the modules.

finding.finding_summary: The MIND-designed microlearning condition produced significantly higher post-test performance than the ADDIE control after adjusting for pre-test scores, F(1,61)=45.976, p<.001, partial η2=.430. In the experimental group (n=32), the post-test mean was 86.000 (SD=6.932) versus 79.312 (SD=5.038) in the control group (n=32), indicating improved knowledge acquisition, comprehension, and application in an AI research-skills course.
finding.measure: Pre-test/post-test multiple-choice assessment of GenAI knowledge, AI applications in research, and AI ethics
finding.std_deviation: Experimental post-test SD=6.932; control post-test SD=5.038

finding.finding_summary: Learner reflections indicated improvements in engagement, motivation, satisfaction, self-concept, and perceived accessibility of the microlearning experience. Although these were qualitative findings rather than a standardized scale, they consistently supported the quantitative gains and suggested the AI-integrated design improved learners' willingness and confidence to learn.
finding.measure: Thematic analysis of learner reflections on engagement, motivation, satisfaction, and self-concept

finding.finding_summary: Qualitative reflections reported gains in problem-solving skills, research skills, knowledge application, and comprehension. These outcomes were supported by the post-test gains and suggest the microlearning intervention helped learners apply AI tools to real tasks, although no separate standardized durable-skills measure was reported.
finding.measure: Thematic analysis of reflections; course post-test items on application and AI research skills
finding.study_size: n=32 reflections in experimental group; n=64 for post-test comparison

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that the MIND model was more time- and cost-efficient than ADDIE because AI tools streamlined content generation, refinement, and instructional design. This outcome is based on author interpretation and participant feedback about ease of access and compact delivery, not a formal productivity metric.
finding.measure: Qualitative reports of ease of design/delivery, accessibility, and reduced cognitive overload; author comparison of design process efficiency
